lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Add a concise summary or role-focused heading.
items.because: The résumé starts with education, so readers have to infer the quantitative-research target later.

items.says: Make the statistical-research-to-systematic-finance thread apparent earlier.
items.because: The strong quant narrative starts late, while the current bakery role can distract from it.

items.says: Consider shortening the bakery experience.
items.because: It takes attention away from the target field.

items.says: Put the clearest, best-validated Northpeak outcome first, with supporting evidence nearby.
items.because: The strongest result is near the bottom of the internship entry.

items.says: Clarify the scale or outcome of the weekly labour-budget responsibility.
items.because: It currently reads as a responsibility claim rather than a measurable result.

items.says: Use a spelling convention consistent with the rest of the résumé for “labour.”
items.because: The U.S. location alongside “labour” may look inconsistent.

items.says: Clarify the basis for the 12%-to-7% unsold-bread comparison.
items.because: The reduction needs a clear basis.

items.says: Clarify whether the unsold-bread reduction was attributable to your changes.
items.because: The review says the result should be attributable to your work.

items.says: Specify what the 35% measures, its comparison, test period, and evaluation setting.
items.because: A large performance improvement is difficult to interpret without that context.

items.says: Keep the validation evidence close to the performance claim it supports.
items.because: The split design and embargo help establish how the backtest addressed leakage.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to the feature store.
items.because: The bullet does not make your individual contribution fully clear.

items.says: Explain what reuse in two later signal projects involved.
items.because: That adoption is stronger evidence of impact than simply building the store.

items.says: Clarify whether the live allocation followed a research review.
items.because: The decision-maker response would be more precise.

items.says: Explain what “small” means if it can be shared.
items.because: The allocation’s scale is unclear.

items.says: Do not present the best Sharpe from 400 selected configurations as an expected live Sharpe without further support.
items.because: Treating a selected backtest result as a forward expectation raises overfitting and credibility concerns.

items.says: The 18-month order-book signal result appears again in the Kaggle project.
items.because: It may present the same work twice as though it were separate evidence.

items.says: Make the Sharpe comparison and testing period directly interpretable.
items.because: Readers need to understand the basis of the reported performance result.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker may invalidate the Monte Carlo replications.
items.because: Identical seeds can produce duplicated or correlated random streams.

items.says: Make your role in the proof and the log-factor improvement clearer.
items.because: Readers may need to understand your personal contribution and what the tighter bound means.

items.says: Consider cutting the teaching detail if space is tight.
items.because: It is less central to quant research than the research evidence.

items.says: Be able to substantiate and explain the measurement of the 3,000-download count.
items.because: The scale claim needs to be defensible.

items.says: Clarify the baseline, evaluation period, and forecasting setup for the 7% QLIKE improvement.
items.because: Those details are needed to interpret the result.

items.says: Emphasize the working paper’s status and audience rather than its 12-page length.
items.because: The page count is less persuasive than where the work stands and who heard it.

items.says: Add a specific result or contribution to the feature-engineering bullet, or remove it.
items.because: It is generic and adds little beyond the project title.

items.says: Explain how the 0.02 gap was measured and why closing it improved confidence in evaluation.
items.because: The validation benefit is not fully clear.

items.says: The 18-month order-book signal result appears to repeat the Northpeak internship result.
items.because: The same work should not be presented twice as separate evidence.

items.says: Clarify the project’s timeline and your ownership of the order-book result.
items.because: It is unclear whether this was separate work, work that informed the internship, or the same result.

items.says: Support the Kafka skill with a practical example or reassess whether it belongs.
items.because: The résumé currently gives no supporting example.

items.says: “Time-series econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: A skills-keyword typo can hurt credibility and search matching.

items.says: Make the most relevant methods and finance experience easier to find in Skills.
items.because: The section is brief, while the bullets carry much of that evidence.
